Proactive recovery plan and frontline empowerment

sections.description: Beloved companies repair the emotional connection with customers after things go wrong, guided by grace and wisdom rather than fear.
sections.title: Emotional repair through apology

sections.description: The transcript notes the explicit apology phrase and the expectation that organizations go beyond words by accepting accountability and learning from errors.
sections.title: We are sorry and accountability

sections.description: At key decision points, beloved companies decide to move in the direction of customers, signaling a commitment to customer interests.
sections.title: Choosing the customer-directed path

sections.description: A proactive recovery plan and trusting frontline teams to resolve issues are described as essential to earning customer and employee stories and achieving loyalty and growth.
sections.title: Proactive recovery and trust-building

summary: In this brief lesson, Jeanne Bliss emphasizes that great companies repair the emotional bond with customers after mistakes by openly apologizing, taking accountability, and learning from errors. The speaker frames apology as a humble, courageous action—captured in the line We are sorry—that should be followed by concrete changes and a proactive recovery plan. By choosing to move toward customers at critical decision points and trusting frontline teams to resolve issues, organizations can cultivate deep loyalty and turn broken experiences into enduring customer and employee stories that fuel growth.
title: Decision 5: Say Sorry and Proactively Restore Customer Trust
topics: avoidance of fear in service recovery
